subject: Hosted API p99 excursions — distinguishing SDK retries from server regressions
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fastretail.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: ops@fastretail.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes this afternoon — urgent

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing significant latency spikes around 15:06 PDT today. Our Datadog alert fired for p99 (~2.1s -> 9.8s) and downstream retries from our SDK surged at 15:08. This caused a cascade in our consumer queue and a brief outage of a subset of web requests.

Key notes:
- Region: us-west-2
- Initial p95 jump at 15:05, p99 stabilized high at 15:08-15:15
- Our client logs show a burst of 3x retries per request around the same time (attached screenshot).

We need a quick triage call and an initial explanation — is this a server-side regression or could our SDK/backoff be amplifying a transient?

Attaching: p99_surge_screenshot.png

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Engineering Manager, FastRetail Inc.
laura.chen@fastretail.com

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fastretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 15:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes this afternoon — urgent

Laura — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. We're pulling metrics and traces now. Can you attach a 5-10 minute slice of SDK client logs (error/timeout events) from 15:00-15:20 PDT? That will help correlate client timeouts with server-side tail latency.

Immediate items:
- I'll validate server p95/p99 timelines + upstream infra health (GPUs, node restarts, kernel updates).
- Neha (SRE) is looped in for tracing and log correlation.
- If this is client-side retry amplification we can suggest a short-term mitigation (raise client timeout to 18s and enable jittered backoff) while we diagnose.

Propose a 30-min sync at 16:00 PDT if that works for you.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Technical Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura.chen@fastretail.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 03:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes this afternoon — urgent

Team — initial correlation attached (p99_report.csv) and client-side log extract (sdk_logs.txt). High-level findings:

1) Datadog trace span aggregation shows an increase in server-side tail from 15:05-15:12 PDT but the majority of high p99 points coincide with a 30s window where our ingress saw a 2.8x request rate bump.

2) The request-rate bump appears to be caused by client retry amplification: multiple SDK instances hit their local timeout boundary (~5s) and retried immediately with conservative backoff settings configured by the customer. SDK logs show clustered retry timestamps at 15:08:10-15:08:22. See sdk_logs.txt (excerpt).

3) There are no control-plane deploys or infra restarts in that window. GPU utilization was elevated but not exhausted (avg 68%). No autoscaler events.

Preliminary conclusion: a small server-side latency excursion was amplified by client-side retry behaviour and low timeout settings.

Suggested immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Recommend client adjust timeout to 18s and switch to exponential backoff with randomized jitter.
- Add a temporary server-side request queue depth cap for the route to limit amplification.

I attached p99_report.csv and sdk_logs.txt with timestamps and correlation markers. Happy to join the call.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
SRE, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura.chen@fastretail.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes this afternoon — urgent

Marissa / Vivek — quick summary and recommended next steps before the exec sync:

Summary:
- Root cause: transient server-side tail latency (likely short-lived queuing on a subset of serving pods) that was amplified by customer SDK retries. Client timeouts at ~5s caused many clients to immediately retry, creating a feedback loop that elevated p99 and error rate during 15:08-15:15 PDT.
- Evidence: timestamped sdk_logs.txt shows clustered client retry bursts that overlap Datadog p99 spikes (p99_report.csv). No control-plane deploys or infra incidents found.

Actions we've taken/planned:
1) Short-term (<=4 hours):
   - Recommended customer change: increase client timeout to 18s and enable jittered exponential backoff (we sent suggested patch lines).
   - Server-side throttling: enabled a soft concurrency cap on the customer route to reduce amplification.
   - Dashboard: published a temporary p99 view to Datadog (link below).

2) Medium-term (next 2 weeks):
   - SDK update: ship a default client timeout and backoff policy that is tuned for our p99 characteristics (analysis_playbook.md attached).
   - Platform: add adaptive ingress rate limiting and a circuit-breaker for noisy clients.

3) Communication: preparing a joint post-mortem with the customer that emphasizes shared responsibility (server tail + client retry amplification) and concrete mitigations.

Asking Vivek — want to include this in a brief for the leadership sync (exec note + recommended customer credit policy?).

Attachments: analysis_playbook.md (internal playbook + suggested SDK patch snippet).

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Technical Lead, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fastretail.com>, aditya.rao@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 21:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes this afternoon — urgent

Laura — thank you for raising this and for the quick logs. We're treating this as a joint ops incident. High-level: we do not see evidence of a broad platform regression; the dominant factor was retry amplification from client timeouts that overlapped a short server-side tail.

Immediate ask for FastRetail: please push the temporary timeout/backoff config we suggested to your canary fleet (we included a one-line patch in the playbook). Our team will keep the soft concurrency cap in place for the next 6 hours and run a controlled traffic ramp to validate.

We're also drafting a short incident note for your execs + ours and will share a clearer timeline and remediation items by EOD Monday. Vivek is looped for any executive follow-up and potential consideration of a goodwill credit (if you prefer that route we can discuss).

Thanks — we'll stay on the thread and ping with updates.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
